steps.why: a ≠ 0 is in the question because dividing by a is the step that finds the inverse. If a were 0 the function would be constant and have no inverse.
common_mistakes: Not using or mentioning a ≠ 0, which is the condition the whole method rests on.
Writing (y − b)/a as y − b/a, which means something different.

steps.label: Write the inverse
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the finished function, renamed in x.
steps.memory_tip: Rename the variable back to x: f⁻¹(x) = (x − b)/a.

lines.text: \text{Check}:\ f\left(\dfrac{x\ - \ b}{a}\right)\ = \ a\ \times \ \dfrac{x\ - \ b}{a} + \ b\ = \ x

steps.why: This is the general form of a numerical linear function such as f(x) = 5x + 4 — every linear function's inverse is this, which is why it is worth memorising as a shape.

insider_note: The condition a ≠ 0 is stated because the division needs it, so carry it through into the answer. The method is the same as the numerical version: solve for x, rename at the end.
